correctness.rationale: All quantifiers n>=3 and L>=1 are explicit. Every word has 00 or 11 as a two-position subsequence, yielding M<=2L. The only signatures of sizes one and two are two constants and four edge-singleton minority words, giving 3M-8<=4L. The four classes of three-output words have exact populations n-2,n-2,n-3,n-3. These imply the strict saturation-length obstruction, and explicit construction signatures achieve B(L) with each output incidence <=L for all stipulated parameters. The standard-library checker directly enumerated 4088 words and verified 240 construction cases plus 40 small exact optima.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves an exact, natural extremal question in a high-deletion finite-output regime for every list allowance. It explains a structural phase transition: the sharp code size is 2L through L=4 but floor((4L+8)/3) for larger lists, with the precise first attaining source length. The three-output signature classes and incidence obstruction explain why the bound is attained exactly from that length. It supplies an infinite parameter-family classification rather than a small numerical case.
